messages:
tara.eng: Heads-up — we just saw a cluster-wide uptick in Xid 13/31 on a handful of A10 nodes in us-east1 around 22:40 UTC. Pattern looks different vs prior noise.
mike-infra: Can you paste the log snippets and node IDs?
 tara.eng: Pasting short dump (trimmed):\n```\n[2026-03-15T22:40:11Z] GPU0 Xid 13 NVDEC error ctx=0x7f2a\n[2026-03-15T22:40:11Z] GPU1 Xid 31 ECC multi-bit ctx=tenant-embedder-42\n[2026-03-15T22:40:12Z] GPU0 hot-reset triggered by hw watchdog\n```\nNodes: us-east1-a10-42f1, us-east1-a10-42f2, us-east1-a10-42f3
samira-sre: Noting tenant in logs `tenant-embedder-42`. Do we have recent rollout / load changes for that tenant?
alex-mlops: That tenant switched to our new dense-embedder v2 yesterday and increased batch_size from 16->64 for async embeddings (old traffic was 200 qps -> 1200 qps). Could be correlated.
toni-hw: Xid 13 tends to be decoder/context issues; Xid 31 often shows up with ECC flips but can also be NVDEC. Need card-level ECC counters. @gpu-monitor-bot any ECC deltas?
gpu-monitor-bot: ECC_MULTI_BIT_COUNTER delta: node us-east1-a10-42f2: +3 in last 10m; node us-east1-a10-42f3: +0; node us-east1-a10-42f1: +1
mike-infra: Interesting. Only one node shows ECC jumps. But Xid 13 on multiple cards suggests a software/driver path too. Any recent runtime/kernel updates pushed to that rack?
ops-oncall: We rolled inference-runtime:release-2026-03-12 to us-east1 last week. No subsequent hotfixes. Rollout notes: GPU driver pinned to nvidia-535.54.03.
tara.eng: I queried request traces — failures concentrate on long-context reranks and high token counts. Most Xid hits have seq_len > 4096 and batch_size >= 32.
alex-mlops: v2 model increases KV cache use and memory working set. If multiple high-ctx jobs land on same card, we could hit memory pressure -> soft resets.
toni-hw: Are these nodes on the same pdu/power domain? Thermal sensors?
gpu-monitor-bot: Thermal delta: us-east1-a10-42f2 GPU0 temp spike +12C at 22:39. Power draw +45W. NVLINK errors: 0.
samira-sre: OK: hypothesis list — 1) tenant changed workload (larger batches/ctx) causing memory pressure -> Xid13; 2) ECC flips on node a10-42f2 causing localized Xid31; 3) runtime change interacted with driver/decoder path.
mike-infra: Quick mitigations: soft-drain a10-42f2, move tenant-embedder-42 away from same cards, throttle batch_size for that tenant to 16 for 1 hour and see.
tara.eng: I can request a soft-drain now. Who will handle tenant throttling? @alex-mlops
alex-mlops: I can push a runtime-config override for tenant-embedder-42 to clamp batch_size=16 and max_tokens=2048. Deploying feature flag now.
ops-oncall: Marking a10-42f2 as soft-drained. Added tag `softdrain:xid-investigation:2432109999`.
toni-hw: Schedule hardware diagnostics for a10-42f2 tomorrow AM. If ECC counters keep increasing, escalate to replacement. Also want full memory-test on that card.
samira-sre: Can we get quick telemetry query to show distribution of seq_len and batch_size for tenant-embedder-42 across last 6h? If it spikes at 21:30->23:00 that's good evidence.
tara.eng: Query done — 87% of requests last 6h had batch_size >=32 and 22% had seq_len >4096 between 21:15-22:45.
alex-mlops: Feature flag applied; sending throttled rollout now. Will report when traffic falls below thresholds.
mike-infra: After throttling and soft-drain, we should watch Xid counts for 30m. If Xid 13s stop but Xid31 persists only on a10-42f2, that's clear hardware.
gpu-monitor-bot: Xid events (rolling 30m): 22:40-22:50 -> 12 events; 22:50-23:00 -> 3 events; 23:00-23:10 -> 0 events.
ops-oncall: Nice, drop in events correlates with change. Leaving card soft-drained until post-diagnostics.
tara.eng: Action items: 1) @toni-hw run hardware diag on a10-42f2 tomorrow; 2) @alex-mlops keep throttle for 4h and report perf regressions; 3) @mike-infra run ECC counter alert threshold review (current alert <=1 multi-bit/10m is maybe too permissive). 4) Create postmortem if replacement needed.
toni-hw: Will run memtest + firmware check. If memtest fails, we'll schedule replacement and RMA.
samira-sre: Also add a temporary NRT correlation dashboard showing batch_size/seq_len vs Xid counts per node.
ops-oncall: I'll create the dashboard and add the softdrain tag to incident tracker.
tara.eng: Thanks all. Sounds like combo of tenant-induced pressure + one flaky card. Reopen thread if Xids reappear after diagnostics. :thumbsup:
